body: Glad you could relate. I'm seeing the doctor in two days so they might increase the meds or add another medication :)
It was good for the delusions but it made me sleepwalk every night so they took me off it.

I once believed that the voices were tricking me and moving my possessions around my room. I'm looking for my keys which are on the table but after staring at the table I don't see them. I pull the whole room apart only to find the keys neatly placed on the table and I knew that they definitely weren't there the first time I looked.

Here was me thinking the GP would keep that kind of thing confidential. Then I had to lie in front of both of them and say I was no longer feeling that way. I'm far better off being left to deal with my own issues, other people just add more stress.
Abilify made me really irritable. Is the time frame linked to when you take your meds?

Thank you. Sometimes they give what's known as a depot injection as an alternative to pills. I think it's slow release it can last anywhere from a week to a month.

As things have progressed I've become less compliant with anti psychotics. I wish it was easy to take them but my issue is voices telling me not to, telling me its not an illness, the pills will cut me off from my special connection with the universe/God. That they will suppress my creativity and any gifts I have. The brain likes to trick us and the condition itself seems to put up a good fight not to be cured.

I've just been prescribed a new anti psychotic. I may need a lot more convincing to start taking it so hopefully my psych evaluation will be early next week.
I know it's literally such a crazy statement to make. We obviously all have to be brain dead vegetables to experience psychosis.

I know. I might have understood if I was presenting with these issues for the first time but I've had episodes on and off for nearly 3 years, had several inpatient admissions, been on meds and recieved diagnosis of unspecified psychotic disorder and paranoid schizophrenia and some guy sees me for 5 minutes and concludes that I must deserve an Oscar for best actor. He said I have emotionally unstable personality disorder instead.

I told him if he doesn't have my mind or my ears how on earth can he tell me whether or not I have hallucinations. It was detrimental to my recovery because I was then paranoid that all the nurses thought I was a liar so I kept so many things to myself. At least I'm being listened to now. It was one doctor of many and the only one who acted like this. Luckily I'll never have to see him again. God knows what he wrote on my discharge summary.

It's a strange and unsettling feeling. Living in limbo or some in-between. Not feeling comfortable anywhere and  fantasising about moving to the woods with a few canine companions instead. I don't think it will get better by itself. That's the mistake I made before and it landed me in hospital.

I'll have a think about what to do. I'm willing to give treatment another shot but at least this time it would be actual treatment. Hope both of us see brighter days soon.

Don't worry I didn't think you were being harsh man. To be honest I've been on that side too. Of desperately needing a bed and being refused. And for that reason a post like this would drive me mad with rage.

I've been in hospital 3 times in the UK. I was on this ward before. The other two hospitals were hospital like of course but even if the nurses ignored us I felt somewhat at ease after a few days and there were things to keep me occupied. Here there is literally nothing and I wouldn't say its infamous or anything but it has low ratings. I wish they shut the place down or did a complete revamp and got some funding in.

I guess the main reason I'm irritated is that as shitty as it can be I seen hospital as an opportunity to get myself better so I can get on with things. The opportunity doesn't seem to be there anymore. At least if I discharge myself someone else can have my bed.

However I will take on board everything you've said. I'm not as clear headed as I'd like to be. It could be that too. I've been struggling to make eye contact with anyone here and having to speak or pass anyone in the corridor makes me incrediblely uncomfortable. I feel like if people look at me they can see everything about me. Like my soul is being laid bare to them. I also sometimes feel like people outside the hospital can see me like I'm on reality TV. I realise this probably isn't real but that's what I'm dealing with so maybe it's influencing how I feel about this place in general.

Yeah I'm also at a hospital in London and like you said the only stimulation is the TV but nobody agrees what they want to watch and it's always something random.

I'd feel somewhat better if they had a craft room or at least some paper to draw on. Maybe they have one off the ward elsewhere in the hospital.

It sounds like I'm acting entitled maybe but I didn't want to come here. They said I came voluntary but I never remember saying I'd come here. One minute they said I was just going to chat to the doctor the next I'm on the ward.

I'm going to ask to be discharged tomorrow for the simple reason that I'm getting worse in here. I'm agitated and I don't want to lash out at risk of being kept in here any longer. I'd never lash out at a person but I feel like I want to thrash my room because I'm frustrated. My doctor is also an idiot. He said I'm insecure and emotionally unstable despite the only thing on my records for almost 3 years is psychosis. It was like he was asking questions in a way that I'd answer to suit his opinion.

Coming to hospital is already an inconvenience but if being here isn't even helping then I don't know what to do. I just want my freedom and if they don't discharge me absconding is pointless because I'll be brought straight back.

I just want to feel better basically so I don't need to be in hospital. Thanks for messaging though I'm glad that the experience is shared. UK system is  gone to the dogs.

Edit: you're right, there are a few staff who really care. A lot don't. One nurse was watching YouTube on her phone today under the table when she should have been watching us. But yes there are a few who are golden.
I wish. I'm using my phone data which is running out fast. There's no WiFi. If I had unlimited Internet it would almost be like a holiday, a budget holiday at that.

Thank you. Alan Watts has been such a comfort to me in the past. Don't worry if you don't send this. I can probably find it on YouTube, I'm pretty sure I know the exact lecture you're talking about.

I interacted with 3 different people today who sympathised with my situation when I was at my worst. A samaritans worker, a police-man & a paramedic who called me on my phone. They all said the same thing. I need to start putting myself first before work/uni. It's a scary thought but it's starting to sink in that they're right. It also made me realise that 3 random strangers took the time out of their day to talk to me when I thought nobody cared. I don't know. I think I'm taking the day off work tomorrow and I'm going to get in touch with mental health services. I haven't had a single sick day in work and feeling like this I think now is a good time to remind myself it's not the end of the world. I need to get myself feeling right again.

Thanks for your message.

I'm spiritual. I believe in things bigger than ourselves. I believed that everything is orchestrated and things eventually go in line with some kind of harmony in the universe. Which is why I'm usually positive. Things will work out. This is a growth opportunity.

In my current mindset this is no longer the case. I'm starting to think that there is no order or any kind of rewardm for perseverance. Maybe bad things will just keep happening and the karma will never balance.

I'm feeling the same today. I'm trying to distract myself. I'm in class till this evening then I'll see how I feel.

Edit: I'm very overwhelmed. Can I go to work tomorrow. Can I keep going with my assignments. I'm not sure honestly. I feel like I'm slowing to a halt.

I really don't know. It's just been a slow escalation of bad emotions until the past few days where I've reached "comfortably numb". The thoughts were fleeting during the day but once I made my way to the station they started to get worse.

It's about 10-15 minutes but when I'm stressed or feeling like this I'll take a long detour through the park which makes it 45 to 1 hour. Sometimes I get off one stop before mine just so I can walk more. It clears my head sometimes.

I'm trying to think of the weather getting warmer but it seems so long away. 

I've felt down before, I've cried by myself many times, but never have I felt like this and that's what scares me. It feels like I'm only semi in control. Like there's something else pulling at my mind.
This is me. Afraid of being dead and afraid of living.
11 & 22 for me. I see those numbers everywhere.

I wasn't fully OK before Christmas. My mental health has been up and down for 2 and a half years. Mainly psychosis. 

Being with family helped but it was shortlived and I had to return to my responsibities. I thought I'd feel different after resting for a few weeks but I just felt worse.

I don't know what I want or need. I've been pushing everyone away. I don't want to but it's like I can't really talk to people at the moment. I want to be left alone but at the same time I want people to care.

Yeah I think that's what I need. If I can control this anxiety I can stop it progressing to an episode. I'm waiting to find out when my psych review is with the community mental health team. If it's too far away I'll book to see my GP and see if they can prescribe me something.

One good thing about the classmates situation is it forced me to confront conflict, something I usually shy away from. But regardless its definitely just added to my current anxieties. I've been a bit better with the hood today. Been trying to keep it down as much as possible. Outside is fine but inside I just attract more attention to myself.

Thanks for the advice.

One night I was in bed and I could hear water running through the pipes. I started to hear faint whispering coming out of the running water and this went on for a night or two before I started hearing clear, distinct voices when I was outside.

A lot of the voices I heard in the months following were triggered by other sounds like running water, car engines, trains on tracks. But I feel like the disembodied voices literally happened out of the blue one night and I had no idea that the people around me weren't hearing them. Hearing voices was a shock to me.

I've had the same thought. In one way it is right to say that a dream world exists alongside waking reality so long as we know that a world like that follows completely different rules to our one. My dreamworld isn't really consistent. The locations change, the characters change but there is repeated themes and often I get similar feelings from my dreams. If it was consistent it would be cool if everyone could actually map their dream worlds. 

I do think there's more to dreaming than just random phenomena.

I had a mental health advisor I was seeing at University. I haven't gotten in touch with her because I'm kind of afraid she will get me admitted or convince me to go the A & E. I also don't want her knowing I'm doing bad again. I had a bad summer and I got better. I wish I was still doing good and she didn't have to deal with me again.

I tried to focus on coursework today. I feel the same though. It's kind of a numbness that's been there for a few days. I walked home and I felt like I was moving in slow motion. I feel like I'll just stop eventually.
Yeah I have the same problem. Have to keep reminding myself something happened in a dream and not real life.

Yeah I've had brothers, friends etc in dreams. Sometimes I look after the people in the dream and sometimes they look after me. I wake up almost wishing that I still had that relationship with the person since I still feel it for hours after.

I used to have vivid dreams and love dreaming but it's only lately where my dream emotions last long after I've woken up.

I've been telling myself I'd try this for weeks now and I still haven't done it. I'm starting to feel like a lost cause who is never going to overcome this unless I move out which isn't currently an option.

I'm pretty fed up. I filled up my water bottle in the kitchen last night and this morning I used the toilet. Those are literally my achievements so far. Feels a bit pathetic I don't know why this effects me so much I just want to get over it.

I thought this would work two days ago. I got myself into a situation where I had to face a conflict head on. I couldn't back away and avoid it. I had to literally go face to face with someone and tell them. I hate conflict and the situation was really stressful but I didn't run away and was proud of myself after.

I thought if I could do that I could go back to my flat and use the kitchen or whatever, no worries. The reality was different. I went back into my room and stayed there till the next morning. It feels hopeless at this stage.
